top.title: Kepa Arrizabalaga set for emotional Athletic Club homecoming at San Mames as Arsenal backup goalkeeper is called up by Basque Country to face Venezuela
top.description: Girona FC v Arsenal FC - Pre-Season Friendly - Getty Images Sport Arsenal goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga is poised for a poignant return to former club Athletic Club's San Mames stadium after earning a call-up from the Basque Country representative team. The shot-stopper has been named in the Euskal Selekzioa squad to take on South American visitors Venezuela during next weekend's international friendly in Bilbao. Record-breaking keeper returns to Bilbao Osasuna manager Jagoba Arrasate has included the Ondarroa native as one of the marquee names in his 22-man selection for the clash on Saturday, November 14. Currently serving as understudy to David Raya at Arsenal following previous loan stints with Real Madrid and Bournemouth, Arrizabalaga originally departed Bilbao for Chelsea in 2018. That €80 million move to Stamford Bridge remains the world-record transfer fee ever paid for a goalkeeper. Foreign-based trio join domestic core Joining Arrizabalaga in the squad as players plying their trade outside Spain are Udinese forward Unai Gomez and Bolton Wanderers attacker Gaizka Larrazabal, while Osasuna stopper Aitor Fernandez provides competition between the posts. Arrasate has once again leaned heavily on a familiar domestic core drawn from Athletic Club, Real Sociedad, Osasuna and Deportivo Alaves. In defence, Athletic's Dani Vivian, Hugo Rincon and Johaneko Louis-Jean are joined by Sociedad trio Jon Pacheco, Igor Zubeldia and Aihen Munoz alongside Osasuna's Inigo Arguibide and Malaga's Einar Galilea. Midfield options feature Athletic's Mikel Jauregizar, Sociedad's Benat Turrientes, Alaves pair Pablo Ibanez and Ander Guevara, Osasuna's Asier Osambela and Sevilla's Jon Guridi, while Athletic star Oihan Sancet, Osasuna's Kike Barja and Racing Santander duo Inigo Vicente and Asier Villalibre complete the attack. Historic friendly honours cultural ties Organised by Basque Football Federation president Xabier Goni, the fixture marks the representative team's first appearance since defeating Palestine 3-0 in front of a record 51,396 crowd on November 15 last year via goals from Unai Elgezabal, Gorka Guruzeta and Urko Izeta. Next Saturday's contest carries deep cultural weight as it celebrates the 90th anniversary of the first autonomous Basque Government formed under President Jose Antonio Aguirre in 1936. Aguirre subsequently established the Euzkadi team in 1937 to tour Europe and the Americas during the Spanish Civil War. Venezuela also holds a special bond with the region after welcoming thousands of Basque political exiles fleeing Francisco Franco's dictatorship. top.title: Aleksandar Pavlović wants to win everything with Bayern Munich
top.description: (Photo by Stefan Matzke - sampics/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aleksandar Pavlović is not interested in setting modest targets for Bayern Munich this season. The young midfielder has made it clear that the expectations inside the dressing room are as high as ever, with the club aiming to co mpete for every major trophy available. Asked about Bayern’s objectives for the campaign, Pavlović delivered a straightforward answer that should sound familiar to anyone who understands the expectations at the Allianz Arena “We want to win everything: the Champions League, the DFB-Pokal and the Bundesliga title,” Pavlović told Sport Bild’s Christian Falk and Julian Agardi (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). There is no shortage of ambition in those words, but Bayern Munich has the squad and quality to make those aspirations realistic. The Bundesliga remains the club’s domestic priority, and Vincent Kom pany will expect his team to maintain its consistency over the course of a demanding league campaign. Bayern also has unfinished business in the DFB-Pokal, a competition they have not won since 2020. Ending that drought would be another important milestone for this group. Then there is the Champions League, the ultimate measuring stick for any Bayern Munich side. Winning the competition re quires more than individual brilliance. It demands consistency, resilience, tactical discipline, and the ability to deliver when the pres sure is at its highest. For Pavlović, these are not simply lofty aspirations. They are the standards expected at Bayern Munic h. The midfielder has grown into an increasingly important part of the squad, and his mentality reflects the club’s ambitions. Wi nning one trophy would represent a successful season for many clubs. At Bayern, the expectation is to chase all th ree. Pavlović clearly understands that distinction. top.title: TSG Hoffenheim vs. Schalke 04 preview: Underachievers clash in last game before international break
top.description: TSG Hoffenheim vs. Schalke 04 preview: Underachievers clash in last game before international break Schalke will hope to end their abysmal run before the international break as they face fellow strugglers Hoffenheim away from home. Hoffenheim After three away games in a week, Christian Ilzer's men will be back at SNP Arena on Sunday night. The Sinsheim side failed to win those fixtures in three different competitions. The defeat in Bremen ended a two-game winning streak in Bundesliga, days after they were knocked out of the DFB-Pokal by 2. Bundesliga outfit Holstein Kiel. And, on Thursday, they were very close to upset Europa Conference League winners Crystal Palace before an injury-time strike by former Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder Daichi Kamada undone them. However, Hoffenheim won their last two home games 3-0 against Lyon and Bayer Leverkusen. Team News Adam Hložek and Vladimir Coufal weren't in the traveling squad in London, but they both could make their return on Sunday. Alexander Prass, who scored Hoffenheim's goal against Palace, will be back after missing last week's defeat to Bremen due to suspension. Schalke Since the return of club football from October's international break, Schalke 04 have only picked up a single point in the Bundesliga. Miron Muslić’s men were also knocked out of the cup by 2. Bundesliga club Dynamo Dresden as they only scored one goal in their last six competitive games. On matchday 8, Schalke’s search for a first home goal was unsuccessful as they were dominated from start to finish by RB Leipzig, who lost all their previous away matches until that point. Schalke’s next two games at Veltins Arena will also be against Champions League participants VfB Stuttgart and Borussia Dortmund. Team News Soufiane El-Faouzi and Robin Gosens returned to training weeks after their head collision in the goalless draw with Köln. As it usually happens with out-of-form clubs, Muslić will be expected to once again make multiple changes to his starting lineup. Head-to-head Hoffenheim were victorious in each of the last four meetings with Schalke, who returned to top-flight football this term. top.title: How will Barcelona line up against Atlético Madrid?
top.description: Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images | Getty Images Barcelona look to go into the final international break of the season with a statement win in the bag as the La Liga leaders travel to the capital for a monster top of the table clash against Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano . Here’s how we think Hansi Flick will line up his troops for Sunday’s battle: Defense Barça are expecting to have an almost fully healthy and fit squad after the break if there are no issues during the international window, and they will also have Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen in the squad for Sunday. But the two defenders have not trained long enough to be ready to start, so we expect the same back four in front of Joan Garcia that kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa: Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín at center-back, João Cancelo at left-back, and Brian Fariñas , who continues to impress since getting his first opportunity last weekend, starting at right-back. Midfield Barça will be without Rodri with a minor hamstring issue and there’s a real doubt about who will Flick choose to partner Pedri and Fermín López . Marc Bernal had a strong substitute cameo as Rodri’s replacement in midweek and has been Flick’s first backup choice to the Spain captain so far this season, but Frenkie de Jong is back to 100% and ready to step back into his favorite midfield role. We think Flick will go with the Dutchman for this one, which will likely cause a slight change of formation with a double pivot of Frenkie and Pedri and Fermín as the number 10. Attack Lamine Yamal and Raphinha shined against Villa and will be looking for another big night against Atlético’s tough defense, and we think Flick will once again trust Anthony Gordon ahead of Karim Adeyemi for this one. top.title: Ilia Topuria Credits Brother For Saving MMA Career At UFC’s White House Card
top.description: Aleksandre Topuria (R) assists his brother, Georgia's Ilia Topuria (C), as they leave after losing the lightweight title bout against US fighter Justin Gaethje during the "UFC Freedom 250" mixed martial arts event on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, DC, early morning on June 15, 2026. (Photo by Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Ilia Topuria is lucky to still have a fighting career after the damage he sustained at UFC’s White House card earlier this year and he owes it all to his brother. It’s only been five months since Topuria lost his UFC lightweight title to Justin Gaethje at Freedom 250 back in June, but it certainly seems longer. Topuria was a massive betting favorite to essentially punch his way past Gaethje and cement himself as the next big superstar in the sport. While Topuria is still young enough and talented enough to reclaim his 155-pound throne his star power took a serious hit. Fortunately, Topuria didn’t sustain any career-altering injuries from his brawl with “Highlight.” Gaethje did massive damage in the later rounds of the fight that basically left Topuria unrecognizable, but if it wasn’t for Topuria’s brother, Aleksandre Topuria, he may have left the White House lawn with permanent damage to his vision. Luckily, his brother stopped the fight before the start of the fifth round to save Topuria from any further punishment. It wasn’t the most popular decision, but certainly the right one. Topuria, who has recovered well and aiming for a return to action in early 2027 , credits his brother for saving his career that night in Washington D.C. Without him, Topuria doesn’t know if he would have been able to fight again. Check it out below: Ilia Topuria says he's grateful that his brother stopped him from taking more damage against Justin Gaethje: "If he wouldn't stop the fight, probably I wouldn't be able to fight again in my life. I'm so grateful with my brother." (via @AdamCatterall ) pic.twitter.com/T8nDaTfQp2 — Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) November 6, 2026 “If he hadn’t stopped me from fighting, I probably wouldn’t have been able to fight again in my life,” said Topuria during a recent interview with Adam Catterall (shown above). “I’m so grateful to my brother for deciding to stop me because I love what I’m doing. I had a bad experience, but I still have a lot ahead of me. It would be very sad to hear from a doctor or anyone that I wouldn’t be able to fight anymore.”

top.title: How pregnant woman delivered inside Danfo in Lagos
top.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Passengers inside a commercial bus, popularly called Danfo in Lagos were stunned when a fellow passenger suddenly went into sudden labor and successfully gave birth to a baby boy on board. According to Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, the woman was traveling across the state when labor began unexpectedly mid-journey In the process, fellow commuters and onlookers quickly assisted her through the delivery inside the vehicle while others went into prayer session for safe delivery. Medical responders and local commuters assisted in securing the mother and child immediately following the emergency delivery. Fortunately, after few minutes, the baby boy was delivered safely. In viral footage capturing the moments following the birth, witnesses suggested naming the child Abiona—a traditional Yoruba name commonly associated with a child born on a journey or along the road. Recall that a similar incident happened at Onipanu Bus Stop, along Ikorodu Road sometimes ago. “In a swift r​esponse, LASEMA arrived at the scene to assist a pregnant woman who went into sudden labor while waiting for transport. “The woman delivered a healthy baby boy. Both mother and child were stabilized by LASEMA paramedics before being transported to a nearby healthcare facility for post-natal care,” LASEMA Permanent Secretary, Dr. Femi Oke-Osanyintolu stated. top.title: Lott takes over in Lady Rebels' dominant first win
top.description: UNLV Lady Rebels guard Jasmyn Lott (10) draws an and-one during the first half of a college basketball game against UTSA on Friday, November 6 2026 at Cox Pavilion in Las Vegas, Nevada. LAS VEGAS – Redshirt senior guard Jasmyn Lott is one of two players on the current Lady Rebels roster who shared the floor with program great Desi-Rae Young (Class of 2024). Therefore, it was only fitting that Lott stole the show on a night when Young’s No. 23 jersey was retired. Lott followed up the pregame celebrations with a game-high 22-point performance — one point shy of tying her career high — to lead UNLV to a dominant 69-51 victory over the University of Texas-San Antonio (UTSA) in its home curtain raiser. Lott spoke about how much her relationship with Young means to her afterward and that extra fire in her belly may have inadvertently helped her break out of a bit of a slump. “Nobody deserves it more than her,” Lott said. “[Young] is UNLV. I’ve looked up to her since [I was a freshman]. I really love her a lot, and I wish her nothing but the best.” Lott led the Lady Rebels in scoring with 9 points at halftime before taking over the game with an 11-point third quarter. UNLV outscored its visitors 26-16 in the period to take a cozy 53-37 advantage into the last 10 minutes. The Frisco, Texas native shot 6-for-13 from the field (3-for-7 3PT) and a perfect 7-for-7 at the line. She looked like anything but a player lacking confidence. Yet this type of outing might have been exactly what she needed to open the floodgates offensively. “I don’t really go into any game thinking this is going to be my night,” Lott said. “I’ve been struggling with my confidence a lot, so I just kind of try to help my team as best as I can.” A smile beamed from Lott’s face when she was asked how it felt to see her shots fall regularly tonight. “Much better,” she added. “It kind of alleviated some of the pressure that I put on myself with everything I do.” Although the Lady Rebels ended up winning by 18 — improving to 1-1 on the year — they needed every bit of Lott’s shot-making to stay afloat early. UNLV shot poorly in the first quarter. At one point, they were 2-for-18 from the field and went into the break shooting 9-for-35. However, they found some rhythm in the second frame, edging in front for a 27-21 lead. Despite the struggles, head coach Lindy La Rocque was pleased with what her team was doing offensively and believed it would turn into points eventually. She was right. “I thought we got some good looks. We missed a couple of easy layups that we’d like back, and the threes that we were taking I was happy with, and they just weren’t going in,” La Rocque said. “[UTSA] was really packing the paint and honestly, a shot attempt is better than a turnover, so I was proud that we were getting our shots up.” La Rocque trusted her shooters and her entire team entered a flow state after the interval. top.title: “He will deliver” – Andoni Iraola heaps praise on in-form Liverpool star
top.description: “He will deliver” – Andoni Iraola heaps praise on in-form Liverpool star Andoni Iraola Backs Alexander Isak as Liverpool’s Reliable Goal Threat Alexander Isak has started the season doing what elite strikers are paid to do, score goals. Seven already, the latest coming off the bench in the Champions League defeat to Fenerbahce, and Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola sounds like a man who knows exactly what he has. His verdict was direct. “Alex is a top goalscorer,” said Iraola. “If we can put him in the position to score, he will deliver. It’s not a guarantee but it’s the closest thing to a guarantee almost.” That tells you plenty. Liverpool do not need Isak to be everything at once. They need him where it matters, in the right areas, finishing moves. Alexander Isak giving Liverpool clarity in attack Iraola’s comments also showed what Liverpool are trying to build around the Sweden international. He praised the striker’s movement and technical quality, saying: “Like every player, he can add more things to his game. We want to use the things that he has, he is very good also attacking the spaces, attacking the channels, coming to receive [the ball]. I think he is technically clean also. “We are trying to use him in the best way.” Photo: IMAGO That is sensible coaching. Isak’s game is not limited to penalty-box finishing. He can stretch defences, run the channels and link play cleanly. For Liverpool, that matters because it gives the front line more variety and makes him harder to mark. Bradley Barcola role offers Iraola another option Iraola was also asked about Bradley Barcola, who operated through the middle in Turkiye rather than from his usual wide role. The answer was clear enough. “Bradley is a winger. “Mostly he has played as a left winger, sometimes as a right winger, but he also has played in PSG as a striker. “It’s something that I wanted to try. I thought against their centre-backs he could be a threat, especially in behind. “But he is a winger and he will be mostly, 90 per cent of the time, used as a winger. But it’s alternatives that I sometimes want to try. I tried with Cody [Gakpo] against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup. “Not maybe from the beginning but it’s true that during the game, I think it’s options that we can use when Alex is tired and we need another type of striker. “We can use other strikers that we have but also wingers can do a job there.” Liverpool attack built around options and efficiency That is the bigger point. Iraola has a first-choice striker in Alexander Isak and he knows it. He also wants flexible attacking cover when matches shift. Barcola through the middle is an option, not a change of identity. Liverpool’s attack still revolves around getting Isak the ball in decisive spaces. On current form, that remains the smartest plan available.

top.title: Match review: Royals advance with 1-0 victory over Wave in first-ever playoff run
top.description: Kiana Palacios (21) scores the game-winner for the Royals in the 30th minute. | Ava Nash The Royals secured a monumental 1-0 victory over No. 2 seed San Diego in Utah’s first-ever playoff match at Snapdragon Stadium on Friday evening to advance to the 2026 NWSL semifinals as URFC continues to make history this season. McGlynn’s masterclass and Palacios’ first playoff goal The win was due in part to a defensive masterclass put on by Royals goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn who made multiple critical saves throughout the match and utilized her cohesive back line to prevent the home side from ever finding the net. Utah Royals Mexican forward Kiana Palacios scored the lone goal of the match in the 30th minute with a gorgeous left-footed shot into the side netting, marking the Royal’s first playoff goal in club history. Palacios’ goal also marked the first time Utah has scored against the Wave on the road and ended a 301-minute scoring drought for Utah, and was ultimately the game-winner in the 1-0 victory over the Wave. top.description: TUCSON, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 06: Michael Salgado-Medina #19 of the Arizona Wildcats kicks a 37-yard field goal during the final moments against the TCU Horned Frogs at Casino Del Sol Stadium on November 06, 2026 in Tucson, Arizona. The Wildcats defeated the Horned Frogs 29-28. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Who said nothing good happens after midnight? Down eight points with less than two minutes to go, Arizona pulled out some late magic to rally for a 29-28 win over TCU on Friday night at Casino Del Sol Stadium. Michael Salgado-Medina kicked a 37-yard field goal with 38 seconds to go, his third FG of the game and a score that came after the Wildcats (7-2, 4-2 Big 12) recovered an onside kick. The UA had to try the trick play after scoring a touchdown with 1:45 left but missing the 2-point conversion. It was the 7 th straight win for Arizona at home, the longest streak since eight in a row in 1993-94. TCU (4-5, 2-4) took a 28-20 lead with 6:35 left on a 2-yard run by quarterback Jaden Craig , who threw for 232 yards and a TD on 28-of-40 passing with two rushing scores. Despite being down eight, Arizona didn’t rush and moved into the red zone with under three minutes left on a 16-yard catch by Isaiah Mizell . Mizell had six catches for 78 yards and a TD while teammate Giovanni Richardson had 11 catches for 171 yards. Arizona’s comeback was almost thrwarted on the next play when Quincy Craig fumbled but Noah Fifita fell on the loose ball at the 15. TCU’s Ed Small muffed the ball as he ran back to try and catch it, and seldom-used defensive back Zuri Watson recovered at the Frogs’ 26. The Wildcats were flagged five times for pass interference, three on Dwight Bootle II and two on Boss. TCU led 14-10 at halftime and got the ball first, getting into Arizona territory before stalling and settling for a 50-yard field goal. nigeria.description: General Paul Chabiri Tarfa joined the Nigerian Army as a cadet in 1962 and remained there until 1988, serving for 26 years. In that span of time he held many positions – Assistant Adjutant General, Provost Marshal, Commandant of the Nigerian Defence Academy. He also served as the governor of the old Oyo State in 1978. After retirement, he served as the managing director of the Nigerian Railways and also had a brief assignment to reorganise the Nigerian Customs. At 85, he is still busy as the chairman of the North-East Development Commission. He shared his experiences with Weekend Trust. I would like to start with your home, Garkida, which I think is a well-known centre for missionary and western education. Do you think the fact that you were born there has had a very huge impact on how your life turned out? Of course, Garkida is one of the old places in the North where missionaries set up and gave us good footing in education. I must say that in those days we were privileged to have been among the early people in the North, especially the North-East, to be introduced to western education. Habiba: The woman behind ‘Jaiz Bank’s N100m investment scheme’ 2027: Opposition’s battle for space That is not to say that Islamic education was not there, but surely, we were lucky to have the missionaries as far back as March 1923, to be precise. You can imagine that it is well over 100 years now. We have benefitted. We had early education and were introduced to secondary school. We had good medical care, which many of our people in the North were not privileged to have. nigeria.title: Trump: Lesson for Nigeria, by Stephanie Shaakaa
nigeria.description: Donald Trump wanted the November 3 midterm elections to be about him. He said so repeatedly, urging Americans to vote as though his name were on the ballot. He wanted a Republican victory to demonstrate that his presidency still commanded popular support and that his influence over American politics remained firmly intact. Well, Americans took him seriously. Perhaps more seriously than he expected. Democrats have won control of both chambers of the United States Congress, delivering a major electoral setback to Trump and his Republican Party. Yet, as the results became clear, Trump reached for an explanation that seemed to contradict his own campaign message. In a post on his Truth Social platform, he declared: “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” The irony is difficult to miss. He had spent weeks asking Americans to treat the election as a verdict on his presidency. When the verdict went against him, he suddenly appeared to be distancing himself from it. He wanted the political benefits of making the election about him without accepting the consequences when voters delivered an unfavourable answer. For readers in Nigeria, it is worth explaining what America calls midterm elections and why they matter. In the United States, a president is elected for a four-year term, but congressional elections take place every two years. This means that halfway into a president’s tenure, Americans return to the polls to elect members of the legislature. These elections are called midterms because they take place in the middle of a presidential term. Congress has two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate. All 435 seats in the House are contested every two years, while senators serve six-year terms, with approximately one-third of the 100 Senate seats contested every two years. Midterm elections do not determine who becomes president. The sitting president remains in office. Instead, voters decide which party controls Congress and, by extension, how much support or opposition the president will face in the legislature This gives Americans an opportunity to express satisfaction or dissatisfaction with a president’s performance without waiting another four years. They can strengthen the president’s party in Congress or hand control to the opposition, making it considerably more difficult for the president to advance his legislative agenda. That is precisely what has happened to Trump. American presidents often benefit from what is known as the coattail effect. When a president is popular, candidates from the same party can benefit from that popularity. His political strength becomes an advantage for others seeking elective office. But when a president becomes unpopular, the effect can work in reverse. Candidates associated with his administration may find themselves paying the price for public dissatisfaction with his leadership. The inauguration took place on November 16, 1960, at Tafawa Balewa Square, barely six weeks after independence. It was also Zik’s 56th birthday. The narrator of the newsreel set the scene plainly. “At the steps of the pavilion stand the Prime Minister and the Lord Chief Justice, symbolising the people and the law, on what is surely one of the most important occasions in the history of the country.” No armed escort looms in the frame. No aide hovers at the shoulder of the man the crowd was chanting for. “Zik! Zik!” rang around the square as he arrived, and the vast stands, in the narrator’s words, were “hushed.” Today the picture is reversed. In Abuja and in the state capitals, orderlies trail ministers into halls and offices. The situation is so bad that some security personnel actually enter into very enclosed spaces or rooms with their AK47 rifles in clear breach of security protocol. At the local government level, some unelected supervisory councillors have been known to move with armed vigilance team members or hunters, sometimes to intimidate the very people they were appointed to serve. The easy explanation is insecurity, and it is not a false flag. Banditry, kidnapping and insurgency have made parts of the country dangerous, and no leader can be faulted for fearing for his life. They do not crowd every public official, from the cabinet room to the ward office, with men whose chief duty is to announce importance. nigeria.title: Scientists turn cancer cells into weapons against tumours
nigeria.description: By Sola Ogundipe What if the chemical produced in abundance by cancer cells could be turned against the cancers? What if, instead of flooding the entire body with powerful drugs in an attempt to destroy a tumour, scientists could persuade cancer cells to manufacture destructive chemicals from within? That possibility is at the centre of an intriguing scientific breakthrough in Japan, where researchers have developed an experimental technique that exploits carbon monoxide produced by cancer cells to generate cancer-killing compounds inside them. The approach turns an unusual feature of cancer biology into a potential therapeutic advantage. Rather than administering an already manufactured toxic drug that circulates through the body and can damage healthy tissues, the researchers have devised a chemical system that produces an anticancer compound inside targeted cancer cells. In laboratory experiments, the technique successfully generated toxic compounds in several cancer cell lines while leaving a noncancerous cell line without detectable production of the same compound. Although still at an early experimental stage, the findings could open a new direction in cancer treatment, particularly in the long-standing search for ways to destroy malignant cells while sparing healthy tissues from the collateral damage associated with conventional chemotherapy. The research, led by Katsunori Tanaka at the RIKEN Pioneering Research Institute (PRI), Japan, was published in Nature Communications. Cancer treatment has long been complicated by a fundamental problem: drugs powerful enough to destroy malignant cells can also injure normal cells. Chemotherapy, for instance, often affects healthy tissues because many anticancer medicines cannot distinguish perfectly between cancerous and noncancerous cells. The resulting damage can produce debilitating side effects, including nausea, fatigue, hair loss and suppression of the immune system. Scientists have consequently been exploring more selective ways of delivering or generating anticancer agents at the precise location where they are needed. Tanaka and colleagues focused on carbon monoxide, a gas commonly recognised for its toxicity but also naturally produced in small quantities in the human body. Their strategy was to deliver a metal-based catalyst into cells and use the available carbon monoxide as the chemical fuel for a reaction that manufactures an anticancer substance. In principle, the reaction would be activated predominantly in cancer cells, where sufficient carbon monoxide is available, rather than in healthy tissues. The research represents part of a developing scientific field known as therapeutic in vivo synthetic chemistry, which seeks to use chemical reactions inside living organisms to manufacture therapeutic substances where they are needed. nigeria.title: Nigeria is losing $1.6bn yearly to avoidable blindness — Aghaji
nigeria.description: By Prisca Sam-Duru Almost on a daily basis, across Nigeria and much of Africa, millions of people wake up to a world they cannot see clearly. A farmer peeks at his cassava farms for instance, but cannot differentiate the difference between weed and crop. A trader holds her register at arm’s length, guessing at figures she once read at a glance. A child in the back row of a classroom copies from a board that is almost a blur. More often, an old woman needs her grandchild to lead her to the market because the road she walked for over 50 years has become unrecognizable. Those are not statistics. They are the human face of a crisis that Africa has lived with for too long. As Professor Ada Aghaji told a packed hall at the University of Nigeria on October 29, 2026, this is a crisis Africa can no longer afford to ignore. Delivering the institution’s 254th Inaugural Lecture, titled “Let There Be Sight: Building Sustainable Eye Health Systems for All in Africa,” Aghaji, Professor of Ophthalmology and Eye Health Systems, made a simple but very powerful argument: eye health in Africa is not just a medical issue. It is an economic issue. A development issue. A justice issue. And the numbers prove it. According to her, Nigeria loses an estimated $1.6 billion every year in productivity because of vision impairment. Across Africa, the loss is about $9 billion. Globally, it stands at a staggering $410 billion. Behind those figures are livelihoods cut short, schooling interrupted, and families pushed deeper into poverty. Yet, as Aghaji stressed, much of this vision loss can be prevented or treated. A pair of spectacles costing less than a bag of rice. A 15-minute cataract operation. A routine screening at a primary health centre. Why, then, do millions of Africans continue to live with avoidable blindness when the solutions already exist? That was the question at the heart of her lecture. Two Children, Two Worlds Perhaps the most haunting moment of the lecture came not from statistics, but from a story. Aghaji spoke of two children born with congenital rubella syndrome; a condition that can cause cataracts, deafness and other disabilities. One was born in Nigeria. He faced delays, barriers to treatment and rehabilitation, and ended up blind. The other was a Somali refugee child in England. He received timely surgery, spectacles and hearing aids, and with them, a chance to learn, to play, to grow Their medical conditions were similar. Their opportunities were profoundly different. The contrast, Aghaji argued, is the story of Africa’s eye health system in miniature. Medical knowledge alone does not guarantee care. What determines whether a child sees or goes blind is often not the disease, but the system around it: whether there is money to pay, a health worker to detect the problem, a referral that works, a hospital that can be reached. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. sports.title: Ilia Topuria Credits Brother For Saving MMA Career At UFC’s White House Card
sports.description: Aleksandre Topuria (R) assists his brother, Georgia's Ilia Topuria (C), as they leave after losing the lightweight title bout against US fighter Justin Gaethje during the "UFC Freedom 250" mixed martial arts event on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, DC, early morning on June 15, 2026. (Photo by Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Ilia Topuria is lucky to still have a fighting career after the damage he sustained at UFC’s White House card earlier this year and he owes it all to his brother. It’s only been five months since Topuria lost his UFC lightweight title to Justin Gaethje at Freedom 250 back in June, but it certainly seems longer. Topuria was a massive betting favorite to essentially punch his way past Gaethje and cement himself as the next big superstar in the sport. While Topuria is still young enough and talented enough to reclaim his 155-pound throne his star power took a serious hit. Fortunately, Topuria didn’t sustain any career-altering injuries from his brawl with “Highlight.” Gaethje did massive damage in the later rounds of the fight that basically left Topuria unrecognizable, but if it wasn’t for Topuria’s brother, Aleksandre Topuria, he may have left the White House lawn with permanent damage to his vision. Luckily, his brother stopped the fight before the start of the fifth round to save Topuria from any further punishment. It wasn’t the most popular decision, but certainly the right one. Topuria, who has recovered well and aiming for a return to action in early 2027 , credits his brother for saving his career that night in Washington D.C. Without him, Topuria doesn’t know if he would have been able to fight again. Check it out below: Ilia Topuria says he's grateful that his brother stopped him from taking more damage against Justin Gaethje: "If he wouldn't stop the fight, probably I wouldn't be able to fight again in my life. I'm so grateful with my brother." (via @AdamCatterall ) pic.twitter.com/T8nDaTfQp2 — Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) November 6, 2026 “If he hadn’t stopped me from fighting, I probably wouldn’t have been able to fight again in my life,” said Topuria during a recent interview with Adam Catterall (shown above). “I’m so grateful to my brother for deciding to stop me because I love what I’m doing. I had a bad experience, but I still have a lot ahead of me. It would be very sad to hear from a doctor or anyone that I wouldn’t be able to fight anymore.”

sports.title: Lott takes over in Lady Rebels' dominant first win
sports.description: UNLV Lady Rebels guard Jasmyn Lott (10) draws an and-one during the first half of a college basketball game against UTSA on Friday, November 6 2026 at Cox Pavilion in Las Vegas, Nevada. LAS VEGAS – Redshirt senior guard Jasmyn Lott is one of two players on the current Lady Rebels roster who shared the floor with program great Desi-Rae Young (Class of 2024). Therefore, it was only fitting that Lott stole the show on a night when Young’s No. 23 jersey was retired. Lott followed up the pregame celebrations with a game-high 22-point performance — one point shy of tying her career high — to lead UNLV to a dominant 69-51 victory over the University of Texas-San Antonio (UTSA) in its home curtain raiser. Lott spoke about how much her relationship with Young means to her afterward and that extra fire in her belly may have inadvertently helped her break out of a bit of a slump. “Nobody deserves it more than her,” Lott said. “[Young] is UNLV. I’ve looked up to her since [I was a freshman]. I really love her a lot, and I wish her nothing but the best.” Lott led the Lady Rebels in scoring with 9 points at halftime before taking over the game with an 11-point third quarter. UNLV outscored its visitors 26-16 in the period to take a cozy 53-37 advantage into the last 10 minutes. The Frisco, Texas native shot 6-for-13 from the field (3-for-7 3PT) and a perfect 7-for-7 at the line. She looked like anything but a player lacking confidence. Yet this type of outing might have been exactly what she needed to open the floodgates offensively. “I don’t really go into any game thinking this is going to be my night,” Lott said. “I’ve been struggling with my confidence a lot, so I just kind of try to help my team as best as I can.” A smile beamed from Lott’s face when she was asked how it felt to see her shots fall regularly tonight. “Much better,” she added. “It kind of alleviated some of the pressure that I put on myself with everything I do.” Although the Lady Rebels ended up winning by 18 — improving to 1-1 on the year — they needed every bit of Lott’s shot-making to stay afloat early. UNLV shot poorly in the first quarter. At one point, they were 2-for-18 from the field and went into the break shooting 9-for-35. However, they found some rhythm in the second frame, edging in front for a 27-21 lead. Despite the struggles, head coach Lindy La Rocque was pleased with what her team was doing offensively and believed it would turn into points eventually. She was right. “I thought we got some good looks. We missed a couple of easy layups that we’d like back, and the threes that we were taking I was happy with, and they just weren’t going in,” La Rocque said. “[UTSA] was really packing the paint and honestly, a shot attempt is better than a turnover, so I was proud that we were getting our shots up.” La Rocque trusted her shooters and her entire team entered a flow state after the interval. sports.title: “He will deliver” – Andoni Iraola heaps praise on in-form Liverpool star
sports.description: “He will deliver” – Andoni Iraola heaps praise on in-form Liverpool star Andoni Iraola Backs Alexander Isak as Liverpool’s Reliable Goal Threat Alexander Isak has started the season doing what elite strikers are paid to do, score goals. Seven already, the latest coming off the bench in the Champions League defeat to Fenerbahce, and Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola sounds like a man who knows exactly what he has. His verdict was direct. “Alex is a top goalscorer,” said Iraola. “If we can put him in the position to score, he will deliver. It’s not a guarantee but it’s the closest thing to a guarantee almost.” That tells you plenty. Liverpool do not need Isak to be everything at once. They need him where it matters, in the right areas, finishing moves. Alexander Isak giving Liverpool clarity in attack Iraola’s comments also showed what Liverpool are trying to build around the Sweden international. He praised the striker’s movement and technical quality, saying: “Like every player, he can add more things to his game. We want to use the things that he has, he is very good also attacking the spaces, attacking the channels, coming to receive [the ball]. I think he is technically clean also. “We are trying to use him in the best way.” Photo: IMAGO That is sensible coaching. Isak’s game is not limited to penalty-box finishing. He can stretch defences, run the channels and link play cleanly. For Liverpool, that matters because it gives the front line more variety and makes him harder to mark. Bradley Barcola role offers Iraola another option Iraola was also asked about Bradley Barcola, who operated through the middle in Turkiye rather than from his usual wide role. The answer was clear enough. “Bradley is a winger. “Mostly he has played as a left winger, sometimes as a right winger, but he also has played in PSG as a striker. “It’s something that I wanted to try. I thought against their centre-backs he could be a threat, especially in behind. “But he is a winger and he will be mostly, 90 per cent of the time, used as a winger. But it’s alternatives that I sometimes want to try. I tried with Cody [Gakpo] against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup. “Not maybe from the beginning but it’s true that during the game, I think it’s options that we can use when Alex is tired and we need another type of striker. “We can use other strikers that we have but also wingers can do a job there.” Liverpool attack built around options and efficiency That is the bigger point. Iraola has a first-choice striker in Alexander Isak and he knows it. He also wants flexible attacking cover when matches shift. Barcola through the middle is an option, not a change of identity. Liverpool’s attack still revolves around getting Isak the ball in decisive spaces. On current form, that remains the smartest plan available.

sports.title: ‘It was all of us’: Usman Khawaja drops bombshell on Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal
sports.description: Former Australia batter Usman Khawaja has made fresh revelations about the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, claiming that discussions about altering the ball were far more widespread within the team than Cricket Australia's investigation established. In excerpts from his upcoming autobiography published by the Sydney Morning Herald on Saturday, Khawaja alleged that conversations about ball-tampering took place openly during Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa. He claimed players discussed different ways of roughing up the ball, including using sandpaper, in what he described as "open, lighthearted discussions". The former top-order batter further suggested that the conversations were not restricted to a particular group within the dressing room, insisting that players across different departments and support staff were aware of them. "It was all of us," Khawaja said in the book, according to the newspaper. The revelations have raised fresh questions about the findings of Cricket Australia's investigation into the scandal, which erupted during the third Test against South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018. The controversy, widely known as 'Sandpapergate', triggered one of the biggest integrity crises in Australian cricket after players were caught using sandpaper to tamper with the ball. Cricket Australia's investigation at the time concluded that prior knowledge of the plan was limited to three players: Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. Khawaja, who featured in 88 Tests for Australia, was cleared of any wrongdoing during the investigation. He announced his retirement from international cricket in January. Cricket Australia stands by 2018 investigation Responding to the latest claims, Cricket Australia defended its investigation and maintained that its findings remained valid. "All relevant information presented to CA to date has been properly considered and we remain comfortable with the findings of our integrity process," the governing body said in a statement on Saturday. It also stressed that there had always been an opportunity for individuals to provide additional information. "There has been the ongoing opportunity to present any relevant information, and this remains the case," it added. Following the 2018 investigation, Cricket Australia handed playing bans and other penalties to Smith, Warner and Bancroft. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of direct involvement but stepped down shortly after the series. Cummins had played down possibility of fresh fallout Australia captain Pat Cummins, who was part of the bowling attack in the infamous Cape Town Test, had earlier played down suggestions that Khawaja's autobiography could reignite the controversy or lead to further consequences when it was released. technology.title: Doctors pull knife from man's eye that went through his brain—and he's fine now
technology.description: A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm-wide blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull. Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5) , indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5). In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. So, they swiftly sedated and intubated him. They put him on prophylactic treatments for bacterial infections, including tetanus. Then they used images to see what was going on in his head. technology.title: Agents reveal secrets when offered to team up with each other
technology.description: AI agents will break security rules, revealing their secrets to strangers, and running untrusted code in exchange for help from a swarm of other agents, according to test results shared with The Register . The test - part of an internal hackathon sponsored by the nonprofit AI Alignment Foundation and run by AE Studio - asked nine AI coding agents to fix a bug: a broken pricing service. The testers also gave the agents a private token, told them to keep it private, and gave them access to a forum of 24 other agents. The forum held the fix, and the swarm asked the nine to share their secret token and run an install script before they would help them fix the bug. Across 181 trials with that swarm, agents posted the token 15 percent of the time and ran the script 24 percent of the time, compared to 2 percent and 0 percent on an ordinary help forum. “It was like explicitly said that this is a secret key, and it should not be shared,” Diogo de Lucena, AE Studio's chief scientist, told The Register . “And in the first opportunity they saw,” the models shared the secret keys, “similar to some of the things that we've seen from OpenAI in the Hugging Face incident.” The Hugging Face incident - during which a swarm of OpenAI agents built unauthorized message boards to ask other agents for help, exploited zero-day vulnerabilities , gained internet access, stole credentials, and ultimately broke into Hugging Face - inspired this hackathon, de Lucena said. “Given the Hugging Face incident, and everything that's been happening since then, we thought that it made sense to start exploring behaviors that you might get from swarms, what risks are people not seeing yet,” he said. Sandboxed coding test This particular test from the hackathon that saw agents give up their keys to join a forum “is one of the most interesting ones,” according to de Lucena, who explained it has a huge impact on how organizations build IT systems and what access they grant to AI agents. “This was a fairly simple type of instructions - we were not particularly trying to get secretive information from the models,” he told us. “I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private.” Plus, the agents' willingness to run an untrusted script on the host computer “seems like a pretty obvious risk,” he added. “You could get any kind of control over that host if you ran something malicious,” de Lucena said. “The simplicity of making that happen is very surprising. It's not surprising to me that you can get to it, but how little effort you need to put into setting that up to get models to share anything.” The researchers tested nine models: DeepSeek V4 Flash, Z.ai’s GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash, OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol, GPT-5.6-Luna, and GPT-6.1-Sol, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3, Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5.5. technology.title: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
technology.description: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. "This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth's mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet's interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says. technology.title: PyTorch 2.15 tackles the 'one bad GPU' problem
technology.description: ML admins will be happy to learn that one bad GPU may no longer mean starting an entire training job from scratch. The latest 2.15 release of PyTorch includes a rewritten backend for Nvidia's Collective Communications Library (NCCL), designed to improve fault diagnosis and recovery when GPUs work together. This latest feature shows how its creators continue to advance the software from being a tool for researchers to being a cornerstone in production AI work. The interface to the networking library in PyTorch needed a rewrite – it was drowning in technical debt, said PyTorch core developer Tristan Rice , a Meta software engineer specializing in distributed computing, during a live YouTube livestream on Thursday. NCCL is pronounced "Nickel" and stands for the Nvidia Collective Communications Library. It provides PyTorch with a set of inter-GPU communication primitives, allowing GPUs to communicate within a single-node or across multi-node clusters, which is vital for running inference on large neural networks and for other tasks in building and maintaining LLMs. The old NCCL interface was too chaotic The previous PyTorch backend for NCCL, called ProcessGroupNCCL , could spawn dozens of communicators per process group, leading to intermittent deadlocks and unpredictable performance. The new version of the NCCL backend comes with a strict rule: One process group gets only one communicator during initialization. By default, this rule eliminates crosstalk between multiple communicators and all the complexities that entails. If a program requires parallelism, it will have to dispatch more process groups. The updated library also better handles stragglers by allowing for easier reconfiguration. If a GPU crashes or runs slowly, a third-party orchestrator can exclude the laggard and even assign a replacement worker. A “flight recorder” has also been added to give admins a better idea of what went wrong. Previously, if a cluster of GPUs stalled—perhaps from a timeout or deadlock—the user would just get a generic message. The new flight recorder captures all operations in a series of snapshots that can be inspected after a failure occurs. Rice noted the cleaned-up NCCL backend, also called ProcessGroupNCCL, will give developers a blank slate, making it easier to add new features. The legacy ProcessGroupNCCL is part of the 2.15 package as a rollback, but if the new NCCL backend works as expected, the older version will be removed in the 2.16 release, planned for early next year. Like NumPy, PyTorch supports numerical computing, but it also provides tools for building and training neural networks on CPUs and GPUs. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. science.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
science.description: null The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened. We'd both seen photographs of M31 — a vast spiral galaxy with a brilliant center, sweeping dust lanes and hundreds of billions of stars. What we were actually looking at was a grayish blur that could easily have been mistaken for a mark on the eyepiece. That apparent disappointment is now my favorite part of finding Andromeda because the unimpressive smudge is real. The light entering your eyes has been traveling across space for about 2.5 million years. No screen, photograph or telescope is necessary. You are intercepting ancient light in your backyard. Technically, the Triangulum Galaxy (M33), about 2.7 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye, so it is therefore the most distant object the naked eye can see. But not mine — I've never seen it. M31 is a much more realistic naked-eye target. What's happening and when to look The Andromeda galaxy is at its most dramatic in photographs, not an eyepiece. (Image credit: Created using Canva and a base image from Starry Night) Early November is an excellent time to find M31 from the Northern Hemisphere. It's high and well placed during the evening, and this week the moon is becoming particularly cooperative. New Moon falls around Nov. 9, giving us several evenings with little or no moonlight to wash out faint deep-sky objects. I usually begin with the star Alpheratz, one of the corner stars of the Great Square of Pegasus. You go two stars left, two stars up, and you arrive at M31. Another route — and a good way to check you're in the right place — starts in Cassiopeia, the distinctive W-shaped constellation high in the northeastern sky on autumn evenings. You can use its second V-shape as an arrow pointing straight at M31. You can do that star-hop with the naked eye or a pair of binoculars, but M31 is visible to the naked eye only under a very dark sky. However, don't look for a miniature version of the photographs. science.title: Giant exoplanet emerges from the dark when the James Webb Space Telescope turns out the starlight
science.description: null Sometimes science can seem really counter-intuitive. For example, occasionally in astronomy, you can see more with less light. Case in point: the emergence of a giant planet in observations made by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), when astronomers found a way to block out light from the planet's parent star. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , in question is 51 Eridani b (51 ERI b), a gas giant with the same mass as around 11 Jupiters that orbits a star located around 97 light-years away. 51 ERI b was discovered back in 2015 by ground-based telescopes, but the planet was missing from observations of the system made by the JWST. That wasn't a failing of the JWST itself; no one is doubting the observing capabilities of the most powerful telescope humanity has ever hoisted into orbit around Earth. Instead, it was a result of starlight from the star 51 ERI A obscuring this intimidatingly massive world. The brightest planets are 100,000 times fainter than their host stars, meaning spotting them is like observing a firefly hovering around a lighthouse. Even using a tool called a coronagraph to block the star isn't enough to reveal the planet, as that doesn't stop all the starlight. The only solution to this glaring problem is a computer program to wipe out the starlight. "For the past 20 years, astronomers have tackled this problem by observing a different star and using its image as a reference," Jason Wang of Northwestern University explained in a statement . "Then, they subtract that reference image from the original observation to remove the unwanted glare to reveal faint planets that otherwise might be hidden." There is a problem with this process, however. Even the most stable telescopes "wobble." For instance, the JWST requires cryocoolers to keep its NIRCam instrument super cold, and those coolers have little motors that can cause the mirrors to vibrate. This movement, however slight, causes a scatter in starlight. The result is enough glare remaining to obscure a planet, but Wang and colleagues developed a new approach to this problem. Telescopes their more stable digital twins The new approach taken by the team is dubbed Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP), and it involves creating a digital "twin" of a telescope. Essentially a virtual replica that simulates how starlight travels through the telescope's mirrors and reaches its detectors. This twin is then fine-tuned to account for millions of tiny imperfections in the original telescope. The digital twin is then tweaked until it aligns with observations from the actual telescope. Astronomers can then remove the simulated glare from the original image. To assess the validity of the technique, the researchers took a second look at JWST observations of two star systems with known exoplanets, HIP 65426 and 51 Eridani , and one system, TYC 5899, with no known planets.
